title: Israel's right, threatened with possible electoral defeat, fractures and radicalizes
subhead: Ahead of the October 27 elections, tensions are beginning to surface within the governing coalition, particularly between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. From the right to the far right, political factions are hardening their rhetoric to rally supporters.

After attempted coup in Niger, Algiers unveils new doctrine for military deployment beyond its borders
subhead: To protect its strategic interests in the Sahel region, Algiers sent an air unit made up of Sukhoi and Ilyushin aircraft to Niamey the day after an attempted coup. This move marks a break with Algeria's longstanding tradition of military non-intervention abroad.

title: In Québec, the pro-independence cause attracts a new generation
subhead: More than 30 years after the last referendum on Québec's independence, a segment of the new generation is dreaming of turning the Canadian province into a sovereign country. The movement, propelled by viral social media campaigns, is making its voice heard as provincial elections approach.

title: In Belgium, brewers battle government's new alcohol-prevention slogan
subhead: As part of a package of public health measures, the Belgian government plans to require alcohol advertisements to carry the warning 'Alcohol is harmful to health'. This decision has triggered fierce opposition from brewers and the hospitality sector and created divisions within the ruling coalition.

title: In southern Lebanon, complex Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli strikes leave residents desparate
subhead: The Lebanese Army has sought to deploy and residents have tried to return to their destroyed himes in the towns of Zawtar al-Gharbieh, Froun and Srifa, designated 'pilot zones' in July. Meanwhile, Israeli shelling continues nearby.

subhead: With just seven days to go before the exhibition opens, the director of the British Museum, Nicholas Cullinan, reflects on the extraordinary journey involved in the loan and transfer of this monumental work from France to England.

title: 'The hardest report I've ever done': Photographing young girls sold by their parents in Afghanistan
subhead: The Visa pour l'Image festival in Perpignan, southern France, is exhibiting journalist Elise Blanchard's photographs from her latest report in the country ruled by the Taliban, where she lived from 2018 to 2025.

title: 'Even our ancestors do not remember a flood of this scale:' Nepal villagers face apocalypse frozen in mud
subhead: Warned in time, many residents of Devighat managed to evacuate their homes just minutes before the mudslide killed over 900 people in Nepal and China. They have started to return to the village, where rescuers are still looking for survivors and the deceased in extremely perilous conditions.
